claims.text: `git log -- <file>` narrows the history to the changes that explain how that file came to be its current state, and prints each one's message. It is a simplified history by default, not every change that ever touched the file.
claims.source_hint: git-log documentation, [--] <path>... pathspec limiting and History Simplification; default output format

claims.text: `git blame <file>` annotates each line of the file with the recorded change that last modified that line, which is not necessarily the change that first put the line there.

`find <dir> -name '<pattern>'` walks everything under <dir> and prints each path whose file name matches the pattern; at stage-0 `find samples -name 'Program.cs'` returns samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs.

claims.text: Git keeps a record of every change someone saved into it, each carrying a message from whoever made it; a change never saved into Git is recorded nowhere. `git log -- <file>` prints the messages of the changes behind one file.
